alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:34PM MDT until October 25 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Rio Grande Near Del Norte affecting Rio Grande County.

.Heavy rainfall across the eastern San Juan mountains and the upper
Rio Grande will cause high flows with minor flooding expected at Del
Norte late tonight.

For the Upper Rio Grande River...including Del Norte...Minor flooding
is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande  near Del Norte.

* WHEN...From late tonight to Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Minor Flood. Considerable agricultural
flooding occurs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 PM MDT Thursday the stage was 4.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tonight to a crest of 6.0 feet tomorrow evening. It will then
fall below flood stage Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.9
feet on 06/09/1985.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 10:07PM MDT until October 23 at 11:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Saguache County in central Colorado...
Mineral County in south central Colorado...
Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Several structures are flooded and sand bagging
operations are continuing. Evacuations are occuring from Wolf Creek
Ranch to Fun Valley. Some roads remain closed due to flooding
including highway 160 and FR380.  The Park Creek bridge has been
washed away with considerable debris in the water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1002 PM MDT, emergency management reported heavy rain in the
warned area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Between 1 and 3.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Rio Grande River and its tributaries including the South Fork
area and along highway 160 to Wolf Creek Pass.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 9:43PM MDT until October 23 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.

* WHEN...Through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Ample sub-tropical moisture will bring periods of moderate to
heavy rain across the area from tonight into Friday morning
before winding down Friday afternoon.
- The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147600
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 24, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 24, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 24, 7:00AM - October 24, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
